title: Method-Dependent Blockades of ω-Agatoxin on P/Q-Type Calcium Channels in Slice Electrophysiology
content: ω-Agatoxin IVA (agatoxin) is a highly potent inhibitor that selectively targets P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) and is widely used in neuroscience research to modulate calcium influx. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of agatoxin blockade using two distinct methods during acute slice whole-cell recordings: agatoxin was administered either by perfusion into the slice within a recording chamber or by pre-treatment in an incubation chamber, commonly referred to as a "wet box". Pre-treatment with agatoxin (100 nM) in the wet box for 1 hour resulted in a persistent blockade (a test longer than 30 min washout) of optogenetically activated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (oIPSCs), likely due to the blockade of P/Q channels on parvalbumin (PV) interneurons. In contrast, brief perfusion of agatoxin (100 nM) with artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) into the recording chamber induced a reversible depression of oIPSCs. The present findings suggest that, beyond the established understanding that agatoxin functions as a specific P/Q channel blocker, the method of agatoxin application significantly influences its effects, with pre-treatment leading to persistent blockade and brief perfusion resulting in reversible depression.
